<description>
**Problem:** Snapshot loading doesn't validate the announced coin count against the unique UTXOs loaded.
Repeated outpoints collapse into one coin, so a snapshot can repeat every record, announce the doubled count, and still match the committed UTXO hash.
`loadtxoutset` then reports the inflated count as `coins_loaded`.

Snapshot loading also accepts transaction groups with no coins.
They leave the UTXO hash unchanged and don't advance the coin count, so parsing them bypasses the interrupt check and can delay shutdown.

**Fix:** Compare the announced count with the unique coin count already produced by the existing UTXO statistics scan, and reject zero-count transaction groups while parsing the snapshot.
When both the content hash and coin count are wrong, loading reports the hash error first.
</description>

[2026-10-25] c:6397148633 comment by fametrano (contributor):
tACK e8e8cbcaa25ba75ad04cbacea2ca3d4254bf23d0

A repeated outpoint need not repeat the same coin. I appended a second record for an existing outpoint to the regtest snapshot, with a 500-byte script, and raised the count by one. On the base (cce32b1687) the file loads with `coins_loaded` 300, and `gettxout` returns the original coin: the coins cache keeps the first record for an outpoint, so the content hash still matches. The head rejects the file with "Bad snapshot coins count: expected 300, got 299". With the extra record placed before the original, both reject it on the hash.

The loaded UTXO set is still the committed one. What the base leaves unchecked is the reported count and the extra bytes in the file. `AssumeutxoData` holds no coin count, so this holds for a file matching any hardcoded entry, mainnet included.

I built bitcoind at the head and at the base, and ran the head's `feature_assumeutxo.py` and a small `loadtxoutset` script on both. The test fails on the base at the duplicate case and passes on the head. I can share the script.
</new_statements>
